title: Completeness of inverse limits of power-torsion sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ be a finitely generated ideal. Let $\underline A$ be the constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. A complex $K$ of $\underline A$-module sheaves is called derived $I$-complete if on every slice site and for every local section $f$ of $I\underline A$ on that slice, $R\mathcal Hom(\underline A[1/f],K)=0$, using [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; here $\underline A[1/f]$ is the sheafification of sectionwise localization at $f$ on the slice. The full subcategory of module sheaves that are derived complete as degree-zero complexes is a weak Serre subcategory: in an exact sequence $F_1\to F_2\to F_3\to F_4\to F_5$ with the four outside terms complete, $F_3$ is complete. It is closed under inverse limits of countable inverse sequences. Every module sheaf killed by $I^n$ for some $n\geq1$ belongs to it. Consequently every sheaf locally of the form $\varprojlim_n F_n$ with $I^nF_n=0$ is derived complete; every bounded cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with such terms is derived complete as well. All categories of module sheaves and derived categories are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. No Noetherian hypothesis on $X$, no section-finiteness and no surjectivity of the transition maps are assumed.

source.place: Tag 099Q (proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles), clauses (1), (4), (5), on the pro-etale site; power-torsion objects and completeness are described immediately before the proposition in Section Tag 099P (section-derived-completion-proetale). Bounded-complex consequence by finite kernels and cokernels, and locality from the slice definition.
